items.title: 68163_Tom Whaley oral history interview
items.q: Joe was the one that made me direct the band.

ctx.x: trying to figure out, Tom, -- and I'm a part of this, I'm aware of this. This is the reason I'm so glad to be a part of talking to you and putting your-- having this go into the National Archives. That people will know the importance of one black man that was through all the jazz. You're 86 years old and this is 1979.
And I can't understand how this happened. And I was in Washington in 1970, for Duke's 70th birthday party. You conducted the orchestra which I was in, and Joe Williams to sing 'For My People.'
